product_matched_guidelines.text:
40.11 Sizes and Marks of Tyres and Tubes - Three dimensions are of importance in determining the size of tyres: (1) Tyre width (B) (2) Overall external diameter (D) (3) Rim diameter (d) (Jant, Bead, Rim) which is also the internal diameter of the tyre.

Marking
The "X" mark usually links the overall external diameter (D) and the width (B). The "-" mark usually links the width (B) and the rim diameter (d). For example, a tyre marking of 67 X 11.34-25 means D X B-d, i.e., the overall diameter of the tyre is 67", its width is 11.34" (with a decimal fraction), and the rim diameter is 25". The B-d marking is the most common, but correct marking is not strictly enforced.

Bicycle Tyre Marking
In bicycle tyres, it is customary to mark the tyre as follows: a tyre with dimensions 26X200 should be interpreted as D X B; i.e., the overall external diameter is 26", and the tyre width is 2".

Tube Marking
The size of the tube is usually determined according to the size of the tyre for which it is intended, and therefore the marking of the tube will be identical to the marking of the tyre. Sometimes, the tube fits several different tyre sizes, and therefore it is common practice to mark on the tube all the tyre numbers for which it is suitable. For example: 700/750-14; 550/560/600-12.

Types of Dimensions
The most common measurement is the inch ("), but other forms exist as detailed below: (1) In inches only 7.00-14; (2) Mixed in inches and mm 175-14; (3) In mm only 175-355; (4) In the American system in inches and %; for example, 78-14 means: the tyre height is no more than 78% of its width, while the rim diameter is 14".

Measurement Method
The correct way to measure the tyre is when the tyre is inflated according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Flaps
Flaps are used to protect the tube from the metal back of the rim or from the edges of the rims. The flap is adjusted in terms of dimensions to both the tube and the tyre, which together are intended to be assembled with the wheel. Classification is under heading 40.12, whether imported separately or as a set with a tyre and tube.

Various (Additional) Markings
P.R (Ply Rating) - A marking for the strength measurement of the tyres.
PLY - One layer of cotton.
S.R - Driving speed up to 180 km/h.
H.R - Driving speed from 180 km/h to 210 km/h.
V.R - Driving speed over 210 km/h.
A.S - A tyre intended for a tractor or an asymmetric tyre.
XXIS - A tyre manufactured with a steel mesh or steel wires.
Tube Less - A tyre without an inner tube, in which a special In-Liner is installed so that air does not escape; the distinction between it and a regular tyre is that "Tube Less" is explicitly written on it.

Marking
The "X" mark usually links the overall external diameter (D) and the width (B). The "-" mark usually links the width (B) and the rim diameter (d). For example, a tyre marking of 67 X 11.34-25 means D X B-d, i.e., the overall diameter of the tyre is 67", its width is 11.34" (with a decimal fraction), and the rim diameter is 25". The B-d marking is the most common, but correct marking is not strictly enforced.

Bicycle Tyre Marking
In bicycle tyres, it is customary to mark the tyre as follows: a tyre with dimensions 26X200 should be interpreted as D X B; i.e., the overall external diameter is 26", and the tyre width is 2".

Tube Marking
The size of the tube is usually determined according to the size of the tyre for which it is intended, and therefore the marking of the tube will be identical to the marking of the tyre. Sometimes, the tube fits several different tyre sizes, and therefore it is common practice to mark on the tube all the tyre numbers for which it is suitable. For example: 700/750-14; 550/560/600-12.

Types of Dimensions
The most common measurement is the inch ("), but other forms exist as detailed below: (1) In inches only 7.00-14; (2) Mixed in inches and mm 175-14; (3) In mm only 175-355; (4) In the American system in inches and %; for example, 78-14 means: the tyre height is no more than 78% of its width, while the rim diameter is 14".

The correct way to measure the tyre is when the tyre is inflated according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Flaps
Flaps are used to protect the tube from the metal back of the rim or from the edges of the rims.
